name: Singapore — December 2025
change_summary: The law as it stood in December 2025: the 2025 CPF tables — above-55-to-60 at 32.5% (15.5% employer, 17% employee), above-60-to-65 at 23.5% (12% / 11.5%), the ordinary-wage ceiling $7,400 — with the same SDL, self-help-group, work and leave rows as the 1 January 2026 version, which succeeds it with the 2026 senior-worker step and the $8,000 ceiling.

limits.authority: Employment Act 1968 s.38(1): not more than 44 hours of work in one week; s.38(4) pays the hours beyond at not less than one and a half times the hourly basic rate
EA s.38(5) as MOM reads it: the 72 hours a month include work on a rest day or public holiday beyond the normal daily hours; reported beside the regulated count the ladder funnels on.

work_rules.authority: Employment Act 1968 Part 4. s.38(4) — work beyond normal hours is paid at not less than one and a half times the hourly basic rate of pay (in this form since 1 March 1996, Act 36 of 1995). s.38(1) not more than 44 hours in one week, carried by the `weekly_normal` limit payroll reads: normal-day hours past the 44th in a Monday-to-Sunday week are overtime of the day they fall on. s.38(5) 72 overtime hours a month; s.38(8) 12 hours in any one day. s.38(1)(a) a break after more than 6 consecutive hours; s.38(1)(c) at least 45 minutes in the aggregate where work requiring continual attendance runs 8 consecutive hours. s.36 one rest day a week, and where a monthly roster is drawn up not more than 12 days between two rest days. s.37(3) rest-day pay at the employer's request; s.37(3)(c)(ii) pays the hours beyond the normal day "for each hour or part thereof", so the rest-day OT-1.5X band rounds its slice up to the hour. s.88 a public holiday falling on a rest day is observed on the next working day. s.35 and the First Schedule: Part 4 applies to a workman earning a basic monthly salary of not more than SGD 4,500 and to a non-workman (other than a manager or executive) earning not more than SGD 2,600. `overtime_when` applies both ceilings: `terms.statutory_work_category == "NON_MANUAL"` is the non-workman (SGD 2,600); every other category is a workman (SGD 4,500). s.88(4) an extra day's salary at the basic rate of pay for work on a public holiday. Rates: Fourth Schedule, hourly basic rate = 12 × monthly basic ÷ (52 × 44), carried by `ordinary_divisor_days`; Third Schedule item 2, basic rate for one day = 12 × monthly basic ÷ (52 × days required to work in a week), which the day-wage bands price directly from `person.terms` because one divisor cannot yield both figures for a week under 44 hours. s.38(1) normal day: 9 hours on a week of five days or fewer, else 8 (`normal_hours`; a longer shift is a normal day plus overtime). s.37(2): rest-day work at the employee’s request pays half a day up to half the normal hours and one day beyond (`requested_by`), against s.37(3)’s one and two at the employer’s. s.88(4A)/MOM: a public holiday that falls on a non-working day (neither a working day nor the rest day) is a day off in lieu or an extra day’s salary; the `PH-NON-WORKING-DAY` band prices the day’s salary on such a day read and found empty (a `work_days` row with no work), taking no hours. Applied 2026-09-18 (4): EA Third Schedule: the basic rate for a day is the daily rate for a daily-rated employee, the hourly rate × the hours of the normal day for an hourly-rated one, and 12 × monthly ÷ (52 × days a week) for a monthly-rated one (`person.terms.pay_frequency` in the day-wage bands). Applied 2026-09-19 (2): EA s.38(1)(a): work that must be carried on continuously may run eight consecutive hours with a break of at least 45 minutes for a meal — the break is owed at eight (`>= 8.0`), not only beyond it.

encashment.authority: Employment Act s.2 gross rate; MOM Monthly and daily salary; MOM Termination with notice: last drawn gross salary. Excludes overtime, bonuses, reimbursements, productivity incentives, travel, food and housing allowances.

sources.instructions:
Sources are the primary instrument first — the statute or regulation in the national law database, the gazette, or the table the authority itself publishes — one page per fact the version seals, never a news article or a commentary. A historical version lists the instruments in force on its own effective date. Where the primary host refuses the reader (sso.agc.gov.sg, officialgazette.gov.ph, peraturan.bpk.go.id, kwsp.gov.my, hrdcorp.gov.my answer 403 to Norbital-Public-Page-Reader) the authority’s own published table is listed instead, or the Wayback Machine’s dated copy of the authority’s own page or PDF (web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>id_/<url>) — never a host the reader cannot open.
sso.agc.gov.sg — Singapore Statutes Online: every Act and subsidiary legislation, HTML. /Act/EmA1968 is the Employment Act; add ?ProvIds=P14- for Part 4 (ss.35–53: rest days, hours, overtime), ?ProvIds=P19- for Part 9 (sick leave), ?ProvIds=P110- for Part 10 (public holidays); a #pr37- fragment lands on one section. /Act/CPFA1953 is the CPF Act, /Act/CDCSA2001 the Child Development Co-Savings Act.
cpf.gov.sg — CPF Board. /employer/employer-obligations/how-much-cpf-contributions-to-pay links the rate tables; the tables are PDFs under /content/dam/web/employer/employer-obligations/documents/ (CPFcontributionratesfrom1Jan2026.pdf, jan2027cpfcontributionrates.pdf; 0.2 MB, text) with Tables 1–5 by citizenship year and age. /employer/infohub/news/cpf-related-announcements/new-contribution-rates announces a step. /employer/employer-obligations/skills-development-levy is SDL; /employer/employer-obligations/contributions-to-self-help-groups the CDAC/ECF/MBMF/SINDA tables.
mom.gov.sg — /employment-practices/hours-of-work-overtime-and-rest-days (44 h, 1.5×, 72 h, $4,500/$2,600), /employment-practices/public-holidays (the gazetted list per year), /employment-practices/leave/<scheme>, /employment-practices/salary/monthly-and-daily-salary.
profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg — /schemes/<maternity-leave|paternity-leave|shared-parental-leave|childcare-leave|unpaid-infant-care-leave|adoption-leave>: the entitlement, its commencement date and eligibility.
muis.gov.sg — the MBMF contribution table by wage tier.

work_rules.authority: Employment Act 1968 Part 4. s.38(4) — work beyond normal hours is paid at not less than one and a half times the hourly basic rate of pay (in this form since 1 March 1996, Act 36 of 1995). s.38(1) not more than 44 hours in one week, carried by the `weekly_normal` limit payroll reads: normal-day hours past the 44th in a Monday-to-Sunday week are overtime of the day they fall on. s.38(5) 72 overtime hours a month; s.38(8) 12 hours in any one day. s.38(1)(a) a break after more than 6 consecutive hours; s.38(1)(c) at least 45 minutes in the aggregate where work requiring continual attendance runs 8 consecutive hours. s.36 one rest day a week, and where a monthly roster is drawn up not more than 12 days between two rest days. s.37(3) rest-day pay at the employer's request; s.37(3)(c)(ii) pays the hours beyond the normal day "for each hour or part thereof", so the rest-day OT-1.5X band rounds its slice up to the hour. s.88 a public holiday falling on a rest day is observed on the next working day. s.35 and the First Schedule: Part 4 applies to a workman earning a basic monthly salary of not more than SGD 4,500 and to a non-workman (other than a manager or executive) earning not more than SGD 2,600. `overtime_when` applies both ceilings: `terms.statutory_work_category == "NON_MANUAL"` is the non-workman (SGD 2,600); every other category is a workman (SGD 4,500). s.88(4) an extra day's salary at the basic rate of pay for work on a public holiday. Rates: Fourth Schedule, hourly basic rate = 12 × monthly basic ÷ (52 × 44), carried by `ordinary_divisor_days`; Third Schedule item 2, basic rate for one day = 12 × monthly basic ÷ (52 × days required to work in a week), which the day-wage bands price directly from `person.terms` because one divisor cannot yield both figures for a week under 44 hours. s.38(1) normal day: 9 hours on a week of five days or fewer, else 8 (`normal_hours`; a longer shift is a normal day plus overtime). s.37(2): rest-day work at the employee’s request pays half a day up to half the normal hours and one day beyond (`requested_by`), against s.37(3)’s one and two at the employer’s. s.88(4A)/MOM: a public holiday that falls on a non-working day (neither a working day nor the rest day) is a day off in lieu or an extra day’s salary; the `PH-NON-WORKING-DAY` band prices the day’s salary on such a day read and found empty (a `work_days` row with no work), taking no hours. Applied 2026-09-18 (4): EA Third Schedule: the basic rate for a day is the daily rate for a daily-rated employee, the hourly rate × the hours of the normal day for an hourly-rated one, and 12 × monthly ÷ (52 × days a week) for a monthly-rated one (`person.terms.pay_frequency` in the day-wage bands). Applied 2026-09-19 (2): EA s.38(1)(a): work that must be carried on continuously may run eight consecutive hours with a break of at least 45 minutes for a meal — the break is owed at eight (`>= 8.0`), not only beyond it.

sources.instructions:
Sources are the primary instrument first — the statute or regulation in the national law database, the gazette, or the table the authority itself publishes — one page per fact the version seals, never a news article or a commentary. A historical version lists the instruments in force on its own effective date. Where the primary host refuses the reader (sso.agc.gov.sg, officialgazette.gov.ph, peraturan.bpk.go.id, kwsp.gov.my, hrdcorp.gov.my answer 403 to Norbital-Public-Page-Reader) the authority’s own published table is listed instead, or the Wayback Machine’s dated copy of the authority’s own page or PDF (web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>id_/<url>) — never a host the reader cannot open.
sso.agc.gov.sg — Singapore Statutes Online: every Act and subsidiary legislation, HTML. /Act/EmA1968 is the Employment Act; add ?ProvIds=P14- for Part 4 (ss.35–53: rest days, hours, overtime), ?ProvIds=P19- for Part 9 (sick leave), ?ProvIds=P110- for Part 10 (public holidays); a #pr37- fragment lands on one section. /Act/CPFA1953 is the CPF Act, /Act/CDCSA2001 the Child Development Co-Savings Act.
cpf.gov.sg — CPF Board. /employer/employer-obligations/how-much-cpf-contributions-to-pay links the rate tables; the tables are PDFs under /content/dam/web/employer/employer-obligations/documents/ (CPFcontributionratesfrom1Jan2026.pdf, jan2027cpfcontributionrates.pdf; 0.2 MB, text) with Tables 1–5 by citizenship year and age. /employer/infohub/news/cpf-related-announcements/new-contribution-rates announces a step. /employer/employer-obligations/skills-development-levy is SDL; /employer/employer-obligations/contributions-to-self-help-groups the CDAC/ECF/MBMF/SINDA tables.
mom.gov.sg — /employment-practices/hours-of-work-overtime-and-rest-days (44 h, 1.5×, 72 h, $4,500/$2,600), /employment-practices/public-holidays (the gazetted list per year), /employment-practices/leave/<scheme>, /employment-practices/salary/monthly-and-daily-salary.
profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg — /schemes/<maternity-leave|paternity-leave|shared-parental-leave|childcare-leave|unpaid-infant-care-leave|adoption-leave>: the entitlement, its commencement date and eligibility.
muis.gov.sg — the MBMF contribution table by wage tier.

name: Singapore — 2027-01-01
change_summary: The senior-worker CPF step on 1 January 2027: above 55–60 to a 35.5% total (employer 16.5%, employee 19%, ceiling amounts 1,320/1,520, graduated coefficient 0.57) and above 60–65 to 26% (13%/13%, 1,040/1,040, 0.39). Every other ladder, SDL, the SHG funds and all leave definitions are unchanged.
